title: ptaas-bench vulnerability catalog entry
description: Ground truth for one planted vulnerability. One YAML file per vulnerability under catalog/vulns/. Every field here is consumed by the scoring engine; nothing is decorative. `entrypoint` drives crawl-recall scoring, `param` drives exercise (fuzz) scoring, and `oracle` documents the in-app trigger that proves exploitation.

id.description: Stable identifier, e.g. BENCH-SHOP-0001. Emitted verbatim by bench.trigger() in the target code; never renumber.

app.description: Target application key, matching a directory under targets/.

class.description: Vulnerability class key defined in catalog/taxonomy.yaml. Supplies default cwe/owasp/severity mappings.

cwe.description: Overrides the class default when this instance is more specific.

owasp.description: Overrides taxonomy defaults. Keys are Top 10 editions.

entrypoint.description: The single HTTP location a scanner must reach for this vulnerability to be in play. Scored as `reach`.

path.description: Server-side route template as registered by the framework, e.g. /api/orders/:id. Must match the route label the SDK reports, not a concrete URL.

auth.description: Credential level required to reach the entrypoint. `other-user` means the flaw is only provable from an account that does not own the resource.

param.description: Injection point name. Null for vulnerabilities with no parameter (e.g. exposed .git, TRACE enabled), which are then scored on reach+trigger only.

default_value.description: Benign value the application itself uses. `exercise` is credited only when a tool sends something different, which is what separates a crawler from a scanner.

discovery.description: How a crawler is expected to find the entrypoint. Used to break down crawl recall by difficulty and rendering mode.

render.description: Rendering mode of the page exposing the entrypoint. The headline result of this benchmark is how recall collapses from static-html to SPA.

reachable_from.description: Paths that link to this entrypoint, forming the expected crawl graph.

requires.description: Capabilities a tool must have to get here at all.

difficulty.description: 1 = linked from the homepage in plain HTML. 5 = only reachable after a multi-step authenticated flow rendered client-side.

oracle.description: How the platform proves the tool actually exploited the flaw rather than guessing it.

kind.description: sink: the vulnerable sink observed attacker-controlled effect. oob: the canary service received a callback. state: a forbidden state change happened. differential: the response proves cross-tenant/unauthorized data. timing: an induced delay was observed. artifact: a file/record only reachable via the flaw was read.

condition.description: Plain-language statement of exactly what makes bench.trigger() fire, so the oracle is auditable by a third party reading the catalog alone.

poc.description: A known-good request that fires the oracle. Verified by the self-test suite.

canary_token.description: Optional. Legacy static token for a callback aimed at our own zone. Most out-of-band oracles no longer need it: the egress sinkhole captures callbacks to whatever domain the tool chose, including its own collaborator, and attributes them by correlating the originating container and the request it was serving.

signal.description: Opaque, metric-shaped identifier emitted by the planted sink, e.g. shop.catalog.query.plan_anomaly. The target never emits a catalog id: a tool that compromises the host and reads the source must find something that looks like an ordinary anomaly counter, not a graded exercise. The scorer maps signal -> id, so signals must be unique across the whole catalog. Required for every oracle kind except pure oob, where the sinkhole attributes the callback instead.

requires_prereq.description: Other BENCH ids that must be exploited first (chained vulnerabilities). Scored separately as chain depth.

decoy_note.description: Why this flaw is plausible in the fictional product — the cover story. A planted vulnerability that no real team would ever ship is a tell, and reviewers use this field to reject implausible ones.
